title: Customer Demand Bucketing and Release Crediting Protocol
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: As Redwood scales enterprise signups, PMs must reconcile many high-priority asks from top accounts with limited roadmap velocity. Current intake is first-come-first-serve by signal weight, which causes bursty spikes and perception of unfairness among strategic customers.

Goal: Define a lightweight operational protocol that buckets incoming top-account requests into demand lanes and issues timeboxed "release credits" that represent a guaranteed slice of roadmap capacity for the requesting account cohort. The protocol should be deterministic, auditable, and minimally manual so Customer Success can give predictable commitments without derailing OKR delivery.

Scope: Create the demand-bucketing ruleset, release-credit calculation, intake form updates (CS/AE facing), and the PM operatives runbook for converting credits to scoped deliveries. Also build a small dashboard query (Console) for credit burn and outstanding commitments.

Out-of-scope: Changes to contract/legal terms, automated billing integration for credits, or major Console UX redesigns (we'll use an MVP dashboard query first).

Success metrics:
- 90% of VIP intake requests receive a bounded reply (credit granted / deferral / decline) within 5 business days.
- Customer satisfaction NPS for top-account intake >= 8 (measured via survey sample).
- Roadmap slippage attributable to credited commitments <= 15% of committed velocity for the quarter.
acceptance_criteria: Documentation: Published runbook in Confluence that explains bucketing rules, credit math, escalation path, and CS response templates.
Credit calculator: A sheets-based calculator or small internal script that outputs release credits given inputs (account tier, ARR, severity, strategic weight).
Intake form: CS/AE intake flow updated with required fields to evaluate credits (use case, expected TPS, data residency constraints, reference PRD link).
Dashboard: Query in Console showing outstanding credits, burn rate, and backlog of credited tickets (MVP table + CSV export).
Pilot: Protocol executed with 3 enterprise accounts over one cycle with post-pilot retrospective and CS feedback recorded.
implementation_notes: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Define bucketing heuristics and credit unit semantics. Align with Sales/CS on fairness factors (ARR, strategic partnership, contract value, incident-derived escalations).
Phase 2 (2 weeks): Build credit calculator (Google Sheet + templated inputs). Update intake form and CS playbook. Create Confluence runbook and canned responses.
Phase 3 (2 weeks): Instrument Console query for credit tracking. Run internal simulation using last 6 months of intake to model burn and capacity impact.
Phase 4 (1 sprint): Pilot with 3 accounts, collect metrics, iterate rules. Schedule retrospective and decide go/no-go for wider rollout.
